title: Unstructured Grounding: Chunking Knowledge in Data 360

steps.prompt: An Agentforce service agent must be grounded on 10,000 PDF manuals stored and indexed through Data 360 unstructured / search capabilities. Retrieval quality is poor and token spend is high. Which chunking strategy best balances semantic coherence with retrieval cost?

options.label: Semantic section-aware chunks (~250–500 tokens) with modest overlap and preserved heading metadata for retrieval filters
options.rationale: Moderate, structure-aware chunks keep procedures intact for embedding similarity while staying small enough for precise retrieval and controlled context-window cost when grounding agents from Data 360.

options.label: Embed each entire 50-page PDF as one vector so "nothing is lost"
options.rationale: Whole-document embeddings dilute local semantics, hurt cosine retrieval of specific procedures, and pull oversized context into the LLM — raising cost and hallucination risk.

options.label: Split every 10 characters regardless of word or section boundaries
options.rationale: Arbitrary micro-splits destroy lexical meaning and produce unusable retrieval units.
